title: Ozonolysis and intramolecular aldol of bicyclic ring-fusion alkenes: matching four alkenes to their beta-hydroxy ketones
summary: Four bicyclic alkenes whose only C=C is the ring-fusion bond, watched at two levels at once. On the left a flask at −78 °C takes ozone until it turns blue, then zinc dust and water, then aqueous NaOH on a hot plate; on the right every electron pair moves as a curved arrow: 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition, retro-cycloaddition, recombination to the secondary ozonide, two-step zinc reduction to the cyclodecanedione, the more stable enolate and the intramolecular aldol that closes two new rings, then protonation. Q, R and S run through the same eight steps; each product graph is matched with List-II and the options are tested. No prediction stage - input, run, watch, result.
subject: Chemistry
topic: Reductive ozonolysis of cyclic alkenes and intramolecular aldol cyclization via the more stable enolate
subtopics: Ozonolysis - Criegee mechanism (molozonide, carbonyl oxide, secondary ozonide)
Intramolecular aldol reaction and ring size
Bicyclic ring systems: decalin and hydroazulene
concepts: The ring-fusion C=C is cut: a 6-6 alkene gives cyclodecane-1,6-dione, a 7-5 alkene cyclodecane-1,5-dione
Zn / H2O reduces the ozonide to two ketones (and ZnO) without further oxidation
The more stable enolate forms at the CH that bears CH3 (more substituted C=C), provided the ring it closes has at least five atoms
The enolate attacks the other C=O across the ring: 6-6 alkenes give 5-7 fused beta-hydroxy ketones, 7-5 alkenes give decalins
P → 2, Q → 1, R → 5, S → 3: option C

derivedQuantities.custom_kinetic_enolate: P, Q, S not in List-II; R still (5)

methods: Solved independently before any key was consulted: P2, Q1, R5, S3 - option C

RDKit reaction SMARTS: ozonolysis of each alkene gives one ten-membered dione; every intramolecular aldol product enumerated; the more substituted enolate that closes rings of at least five gives List-II (2), (1), (5), (3) by canonical SMILES
The full eight-step arrow-pushing mechanism pushed independently in Python: every intermediate valid, charge conserved, product equal to the template product
Controls: the kinetic enolate gives no printed option; without base the diones are not in List-II; List-II (4) comes from no alkene
Independent script tests/verify_p1q15.py: 27 of 27 checks pass
Solution websites: MathonGo's published solution (their Q47) gives C

The page pushes every curved arrow on the molecule graphs, checks valence and charge after each step, chooses the enolate by substitution and ring size, and matches the products with the printed List-II structures by graph comparison; no product or answer is written into the script

Answer cross-checked afterwards against the official final key printed with the Paper 1 PDF: Q15 -> C
